Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Hi Tyler Murray, Nomsa Khumalo here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Tyler Murray): I've been on the same rate for years, why is this changing now?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Happy to explain it. Let me pull up your usage first.

Customer (Tyler Murray): Is this the Phase 2 thing the AUC approved, or did I do something wrong on my account?

Customer (Tyler Murray): Can't you just put me back on Rate 1?

Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): To recap: your usage puts you in Rate 2 for now, the class is reviewed against annual usage, and the details are in your email.
Customer (Tyler Murray): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Customer (Linda Fraser): How many months in a row can you estimate my usage before someone comes out?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Hi Linda Fraser, Karabo Zulu here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Linda Fraser): If the estimate is wrong, how does the correction actually happen on a future bill?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Understood. Let me pull up the account and look at the charges before I say anything.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?
Customer (Linda Fraser): Yes, same address as always, and the account's under my name.
Customer (Linda Fraser): Is there a way I can submit my own meter reading instead of waiting?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Can you see the meter from outside, or is it behind a gate?
Customer (Linda Fraser): It's behind the back gate, and the dog's out there during the day.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Do you have a reading from the meter today?
Customer (Linda Fraser): I took a photo this morning. It's much lower than the bill.

Agent (Karabo Zulu): Let me take a look. I've checked the meter-read schedule for the account and confirmed whether a self-read or field read was available.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): When our reader can't reach the meter, the bill is estimated from your past usage for the same months.
Customer (Linda Fraser): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): I've scheduled an actual field read for your next cycle and shown you how to submit a self-read online in the meantime, so this month's estimate will be corrected against the real number once it's read.
Customer (Linda Fraser): So I'll get the overcharge back?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): It's credited automatically on the next bill once the actual read is in.
Customer (Linda Fraser): And the gate?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): I've added an access note so the reader calls ahead.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): To recap: your self-read is on file, the next bill corrects the estimate, and the reader will call ahead about the gate.
Customer (Linda Fraser): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Customer (Chris Young): The furnace makes a soft whoosh when it comes on. Should I be worried?
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Hi Chris Young, Lerato Ndlovu here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Chris Young): Is this something I should be worried about, or is it normal?
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Good question. Let me walk you through it.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?
Customer (Chris Young): Sure, it's the house on the account, and the bill's in my name.
Customer (Chris Young): Should I have someone look at it, or is it fine to keep using?
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Do you smell gas at all right now?
Customer (Chris Young): No, nothing like that.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): When was it last serviced by a licensed technician?
Customer (Chris Young): A couple of years ago, I think.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Is the house heating normally apart from that?
Customer (Chris Young): Yes, it heats fine.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Let me take a look. I've walked through the standard non-emergency safety guidance and checked for any signs that needed a field visit.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): A few clicks or a soft whoosh before the burner lights is the igniter and the gas catching. That's normal on most furnaces.
Customer (Chris Young): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): What you're describing is the normal ignition sequence, so there's nothing to worry about. If the sound changes, or you ever smell gas, call us straight away.
Customer (Chris Young): So I don't need anything from Apex?
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Not for this. A yearly service by a licensed technician is still a good idea at fifteen years.
Customer (Chris Young): And if I ever do smell gas?
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Leave the house and call our 24-hour emergency line from outside.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): To recap: the ignition sound is normal, a yearly service is worth booking, and the emergency line is there if you ever smell gas.
Customer (Chris Young): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Customer (Mark Douglas): I'm following up again — I'm moving next week and need gas stopped at my old place and started at the new one.

Customer (Mark Douglas): I already explained this on my last contact.

Customer (Mark Douglas): What's the actual turnaround time between the stop and the start?

Customer (Mark Douglas): It's an old one. Can you change it to my new email?

Customer (Mark Douglas): Yes, same bank as now.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Let me take a look. I've processed the account request and confirmed the effective date against the service address change.

Agent (Naledi Nkosi): To recap: the stop is booked, the new meter needs a technician visit, and you're on the priority list for an earlier slot.
Customer (Mark Douglas): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
